Instructions from: /home/pixel/code/htb-2026/web/AGENTS.md
# Web app

The web app is a Next.js 16 project (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, ESLint), managed with pnpm. Run commands from `web/`:

- `pnpm dev`: dev server on http://localhost:3000
- `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck`: run before each commit
- `pnpm build`: also run before committing a change to config, dependencies, routing, data fetching or server code. Skip it for changes confined to component markup and styling.

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill it in before running the app. It lists the AI Gateway key that Jev's audience scoring needs; without it, scoring falls back to keyword matching.

## Next.js version

Next.js 16 has breaking changes from earlier versions in APIs, conventions and file structure, so code written from memory of Next.js 15 or older may not work. Before writing routing, data-fetching, caching or config code, read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, which matches the installed version. Breaking changes from 15 are listed in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/upgrading/version-16.md`.

`agentRules: false` in `next.config.ts` stops `next dev` from writing its own block of agent instructions into this file.

## UI

UI components come from shadcn/ui (`base-nova` style, on Base UI). Add one with `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>` from `web/`; it lands in `src/components/ui/`.

Load the `frontend-design` skill before UI work. It is vendored from Anthropic's `claude-plugins-official` marketplace, under the Apache 2.0 licence in its folder, `.agents/skills/frontend-design/` at the repository root.

## LLM calls

LLM calls and AI agents go through the Vercel AI SDK (`ai` plus a provider package), not a provider's own SDK.

## Checking frontend work

- Check a change to behaviour, data flow or layout on the running dev server with Playwright or a browser before reporting it done: look at the page, use the changed flow, and read the console for errors.
- Skip the browser check for a cosmetic change confined to one component, such as a colour, text, spacing or icon. Say in the reply that it wasn't checked in the browser.
- Before starting a dev server, check whether one is already running, by its process or by probing its port, and reuse it. A change to config, dependencies or env means stopping it and starting a fresh one. Never leave several instances running.

The bug: clicking a placement in the list triggers flyTo + scrollIntoView. But the effect depends on `selected` and `placements`. If placements array identity changes (e.g., data refetch/re-render), the effect re-runs and scrolls back — "sucking you back". Also flyTo is fired every time. The scrollIntoView on mobile is the likely culprit: it scrolls map into view, which then... hmm "keep sucking you back to it" — clicking placement to buy focuses map, then you scroll back to list and it pulls you back again? That would happen if effect re-runs due to placements array identity change.

Also note `focus.select` always sets a new object with Date.now(), but that only happens on click.

Let me read the rest of tract-map and PlacementsSection to see how placements data changes. Also check use-audience-run for polling that recreates placements.

Actually likely cause: `placements` prop is a new array each render or updated by polling (audience run polling placements found so far). Then effect re-runs with same selected and yanks back. Fix: track the last handled selection (id + at) in a ref, so each click handled once.

Also should not run scrollIntoView if already in view perhaps, but the once-only guard is the core fix.

Let me check whether placements gets updated over time.

Actually cleaner: guard on `selected.at` only in a ref, since `at` is unique per selection and changes with every click. Use `lastHandled` ref storing `number | null`. But if user clicks map then list... `at` differs each click anyway. Use `${selected.id}:${selected.at}`.

Let's edit.

Found it. The map effect at `tract-map.tsx:104` depends on `placements`, and that array gets a new identity on every run update (each agent event → `useAudienceRun`'s `ordered` memo rebuilds it). So while the run is still streaming, each event re-fires `flyTo` + `scrollIntoView` for the same selection, dragging you back. The campaign effect has the same flaw.

The fix: remember which click was already handled, keyed by the selection's unique `at` timestamp.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Create screenshots directory if it doesn't exist
SCREENSHOT_DIR="$HOME/screenshots"
mkdir -p "$SCREENSHOT_DIR"

# Generate filename with timestamp
FILENAME="$SCREENSHOT_DIR/screenshot_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).png"

case "${1:-area}" in
  area)
    # Area selection screenshot
    grim -g "$(slurp)" "$FILENAME"
    ;;
  screen)
    # Full screen screenshot
    grim "$FILENAME"
    ;;
  window)
    # Active window screenshot
    grim -g "$(hyprctl activewindow -j | jq -r '"\(.at[0]),\(.at[1]) \(.size[0])x\(.size[1])"')" "$FILENAME"
    ;;
  edit)
    # Take area screenshot and open in swappy for editing
    grim -g "$(slurp)" - | swappy -f -
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Usage: $0 [area|screen|window|edit]"
    echo "  area   - Select area to screenshot (default)"
    echo "  screen - Full screen screenshot"
    echo "  window - Active window screenshot"
    echo "  edit   - Select area and edit with swappy"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# Copy to clipboard
wl-copy < "$FILENAME"
